question: Will Russian, Ukrainian, and US officials hold a trilateral negotiation meeting between October 15 and 17, 2026?

calls.reasoning: As of Oct 6, 2026 no date is fixed: the US proposes technical-level trilateral talks 'by the end of October' (Zelensky, Oct 3-4), with the UAE/Abu Dhabi the likely venue. Ukraine has agreed and the Kremlin has said October 'cannot be ruled out', but there is no Russian confirmation of a date. Polymarket's 'any diplomatic meeting' market (about $428k total volume, a looser contract than this question) prices ~23% by Oct 15 and ~58% by Oct 31. That points to about 30-35% for a meeting between Oct 15 and Oct 31, and a 3-day slice of that gives about 6-8%. A round starting Oct 14 and running into the 15th adds a little; Russia's history of slow-walking and nothing pointing to mid-October in particular pull it down.

- Kyiv Independent, 2026-10-04: Zelensky says the US is proposing 'some kind of meeting at the technical level in a trilateral format by the end of October'; Ukraine is willing and open to the UAE or another US-proposed country; no date, format or agenda finalized; no Russian acceptance reported in the article.
- Censor.net citing The Atlantic, 2026-09-29: US intends to arrange a Ukraine-Russia meeting in Abu Dhabi in October to discuss a limited ceasefire (energy infrastructure, Black Sea shipping); Ukrainian sources do not expect serious Putin engagement before spring 2027.
- Kommersant, Vedomosti and Meduza, 2026-09-13: Peskov says trilateral talks could resume in October ('cannot be ruled out'); Ushakov calls Abu Dhabi acceptable; no date set.
- RFE/RL and Pravda, late Sep 2026: Peskov says there are no preconditions for a 'peace track' but repeats that Zelensky could come to Moscow.
- UK Commons Library briefing: UAE talks 'proposed and accepted in principle', expected October 2026, date not agreed.
- Moscow Times and Pravda, 2026-10-03: US-Russia track also involves a Lukoil asset deal (NYT report).
- CNBC, 2026-10-05: Russia ramps up attacks as the US pushes for talks.
- Past rounds in 2026: Abu Dhabi Jan 23-24, Abu Dhabi Feb 4-5, Geneva Feb 17-18 (each about 2 days, dates announced about 1 week to a few days ahead); none since late February.
- Human markets: Polymarket has a cumulative-deadline 'Russia x Ukraine any diplomatic meeting by...' ladder (Oct 15 / Oct 31 / Dec 31 contracts) with a broader definition than this question; no market found for an Oct 15-17 in-person trilateral meeting.
- Status quo: no meeting scheduled as of Oct 6.
- Resolves off credible reports of an in-person meeting with all three governments in the same room; not bilateral US-Russia or US-Ukraine meetings, calls, or shuttle diplomacy.
- Event window: Oct 15 00:00 UTC -> Oct 17 23:59 UTC, 2026; as of Oct 6, 0% elapsed (window opens in about 9 days). A meeting that starts earlier counts if it is still in session on Oct 15.
- Searched for but not found: any specific announced date, any 'mid-October' report, Russian confirmation of the end-of-October target, Kalshi or bookmaker markets.

calls.reasoning: As of Oct 6, 2026 no trilateral date or venue has been set. Per Zelensky on Oct 4, the US is proposing a technical-level three-way meeting 'by the end of October' or 'in late October', most likely in the UAE. Kyiv Independent reported on Oct 5 that an early-October expectation had already slipped to late October and that Moscow is reluctant to commit. The three 2026 rounds were each announced about 3-10 days ahead, so a meeting on Oct 15-17 would need an announcement within days. P(a trilateral round in October) looks like about 30-35%. Since the target is late October, the share of that falling on Oct 15-17 is below the 3-of-25-days uniform share, which puts the estimate around 4-6%. No market matches this contract: Polymarket's broader any-meeting/whole-month contracts are evidence only.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the facts: no date is set, the US proposes technical-level talks by or in late October, Ukraine is willing, and Russia has not confirmed. The one apparent factual gap is phrasing: Run 1 and Run 2 cite 'by the end of October', while Run 3 cites 'late October' plus the Oct 5 Kyiv Independent report of slippage. These are compatible, and both point away from mid-month. The Polymarket figures differ because they come from different dates and different contracts (Run 1: ~23% by Oct 15 and ~58% by Oct 31; Run 2/3: ~48.5% on Sept 27). I cannot check these without web access, and since all of them are near-miss contracts they are not anchors anyway. The rest is judgment about how much of the October probability lands on Oct 15-17. A late-October target and no announcement 9 days out argue for the low end, so I land at 5%.
